title: Become an Elusive Object of Desire: The Law of Covetousness
coreMove: Shape desire by withholding complete access, creating room for projection, and refusing to beg for attention.
sourcePressure: This law argues desire intensifies around distance, scarcity, projection, and rivalry wherever status, attention, opportunity, or possession feels contested.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating covetousness as manipulation or romance only, instead of understanding how distance and scarcity structure wanting.

exampleSpecs.domain: an indie game studio showing a closed prototype at a convention
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder tempted to explain every mechanic
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether curiosity survives past a crowded booth
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the founder lets players see one locked character silhouette and stops explaining, so the line forms around what they cannot yet access
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a demo screen with one character slot blacked out

exampleSpecs.domain: a rare-book dealer deciding how much provenance to reveal before auction
exampleSpecs.audience: a seller balancing trust and imagination
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether bidders feel discovery or feel managed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she shows the marginal note and binding repair, then withholds the full ownership story until the catalog date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a linen-covered table with a cracked leather spine resting on foam

exampleSpecs.domain: a jazz trio booking a residency in a crowded club market
exampleSpecs.audience: a bandleader learning that overavailability cheapens demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the room becomes a habit or an event
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the band shifts from weekly filler slots to three announced nights with one unreleased arrangement held for the final set
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass set list clipped to a piano lid

exampleSpecs.domain: a fellowship program trying to attract overcommitted researchers
exampleSpecs.audience: a program director designing selective access without arrogance
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the offer feels prestigious or bureaucratic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director predicts more details will reassure applicants, then sees the shorter invitation with one hard constraint produce stronger responses
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sealed invitation envelope beside a one-page criteria sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: a ceramic artist whose work stops selling after she floods every market stall
exampleSpecs.audience: a maker learning the cost of full availability
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether buyers keep postponing because the bowl will always be there
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares months with unlimited stock against a small numbered release and sees desire return with real limits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six numbered bowls lined on a raw wood shelf

exampleSpecs.domain: a campaign strategist deciding when to reveal a candidate's policy endorsement
exampleSpecs.audience: a political aide resisting premature saturation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether attention peaks before the vote or burns out early
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the aide argues for holding the endorsement until opponents commit, making the late reveal feel consequential instead of needy
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blank podium placard in an empty press room

skillTargets: distinguish healthy mystery from needy withholding
